reference.citation: Yilmaz R et al. (2022). Continuous monitoring of surgical bimanual expertise using deep neural networks in virtual reality simulation. npj Digital Medicine 5, 54.
reference.adaptation: Feature selection and 0.2-second reporting inspiration; original implementation, no transferred classifier or reference thresholds.

provenance.time: simulated elapsed seconds; successful engine microsteps, not wall clock
provenance.pose: model-derived committed tool-tip RAS+ millimeters and xyzw unit quaternion
provenance.active: effective activation during the observed microstep; latchedActive records the persistent switch separately
provenance.motion: finite differences of committed microstep poses with actual dt; path excludes placement jumps; unavailable derivatives are null
provenance.sampling: last observation at or before each reporting time, no interpolation; observedTimeSeconds and observationAgeSeconds expose staleness
provenance.force: forceAssumedN is the declared simulator parameter/default, never a measured contact force; measuredForceN is unknown (null)
provenance.removal: model-derived whole-cell removal, using explicit target membership and affine voxel volume; non-target includes access bone and other materials, not a healthy-tissue injury label
provenance.woundsAndFluid: model-derived under declared research assumptions; fluid includes irrigation and modeled sources, not measured blood loss
provenance.contact: model-derived cumulative cell-seconds; exposureByMaterialCellSeconds follows engine working-contact accounting, not complete per-hand force sensing
provenance.events: committed microstep events have observed simulation times; rejection/contact-stop and exchange outcomes are action-boundary events
provenance.injuryAndExpertise: clinical injury, patient risk, and expertise are unknown; no score inferred
